_comment: Accepted findings of the Semgrep registry packs gated by scripts/check-semgrep-packs.sh. Each entry matches one finding by rule, path and the trimmed source line it points at; when that line changes the entry goes stale and the gate fails until it is re-reviewed. Product sources cannot carry nosemgrep comments for a registry pack without the pack being part of their review, so the reasons live here.

ignores.reason: Local profiling example: argv[1..] are row counts and file paths typed by the developer running it. argv[0] is skipped and nothing is a security decision.
Local profiling example: reads a row count from the command line; a bad value only changes the size of the synthetic workload.
Local profiling example: argv[1..] select the input file and run count; argv[0] is skipped and nothing is a security decision.
Evidence tooling run by make dependency-evidence: the argument is the repository root to hash, supplied by the repo's own script. It grants no access the caller does not already have.
Local profiling example: argv[1..] are the CSV path and options of a developer-run benchmark; argv[0] is skipped.

Native-only payload spill directory. It is created with DirBuilder::create (not create_all), mode 0o700, under a pid+counter name, and the loop retries on AlreadyExists, so a pre-planted directory or symlink is never adopted. The browser build spills to OPFS, not here.
secure_zero_bytes: a volatile store through an exclusive &mut u8 so the optimizer cannot drop the wipe of sensitive bytes. The SAFETY comment above it states the invariant.

ignores.match: let res = unsafe { lprofWriteData(&mut writer, core::ptr::null_mut(), 0) };
ignores.reason: footprint_capture is compiled only with the dependency-campaign-bootstrap feature (evidence WASM, never the shipped package). It calls the linked LLVM profile runtime with a NULL value-profile reader, which the runtime documents as a no-op.

Integration test re-runs its own test binary once as a fresh process (a cold OnceLock) to compare output bytes. Only the test harness runs it; the path grants nothing the developer running cargo test does not already have, and nothing ships.

Local profiling example: reads this process's resident-set high-water mark from libc getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) into an exclusively borrowed repr(C) struct with the 64-bit macOS/Linux struct rusage layout; compiled only for 64-bit unix. Nothing shipped; the value is only printed.

Local profiling example: libc getloadavg writes at most the three doubles requested into a three-element array, so each published timing records the system load it ran under. Nothing shipped; the value is only printed.
